13be515e46a6.summary_en: NME ’s latest stars of The Cover , Radio Free Alice , have created an exclusive playlist to accompany the story’s launch – check it out below. READ MORE: Radio Free Alice are ready to take on the world The Australian indie band are on this week’s (October 19) edition of The Cover , a manifestation of NME ’s commitment to supporting emerging talent across the globe on a weekly basis. Every week, a rising artist will feature on The Cover – you can read Radio Free Alice’s profile here , written by Jordan Bassett and featuring photography by Tom Oxley. The four-piece have curated an exclusive playlist to accompany their appearance on The Cover , titled ‘Melbourne Friends’. The collection features artists from their local scene, including Dumbhead, Rain Dogs, HighSchool , former The Cover stars The Belair Lip Bombs , and more. Listen to the full playlist on Spotify below and on Apple Music . Radio Free Alice are set to release their debut album ‘What’s In Between’ on October 30, and in The Cover , they discuss their path to their first album – a journey that started when frontman Noah Learmonth and guitarist Jules Paradiso met as teenagers. “When you’re 14, 15, having someone that you can freely play music with or fuck around with is so important and exciting, as opposed to just doing it yourself,” Paradiso recalls of when the pair first started collaborating. “After a few years of doing it together, you start to realise: ‘Oh, shit, OK – maybe there’s a little nugget of something that we can actually move forward with.’” The band have evolved into an ambitious prospect – one that isn’t afraid to really go for their goals. “There’s a lot of people who don’t want to say they wanna be a really big band and then not be a big band and feel awkward about it,” explains Learmonth. “But then, as a result, no one manifests it, and everyone’s just making cassette tapes played in share houses to hipsters, so they’re not getting big. It’s this self-fulfilling prophecy. We never felt that we had to pretend not to be ambitious because there’s too many people in our genre pretending not to be.” Read Radio Free Alice’s full Cover story here and find out who else has been on The Cover here . Every year, NME produces 50 Cover stories, showcasing the future of music via in-depth profiles and exclusive photoshoots. Check out our coffee table book NME The Cover 2024-2025 , which features the likes of Kneecap , Lola Young , Amaarae , LE SSERAFIM , Oklou and many more. The post Radio Free Alice shout out their ‘Melbourne Friends’ in exclusive playlist to accompany The Cover appeared first on NME .

Плейлист приурочен к их выпуску в рубрике The Cover от NME.
13be515e46a6.title: Radio Free Alice shout out their ‘Melbourne Friends’ in exclusive playlist to accompany The Cover

9a72aece7356.summary_en: Doves ‘ Jez Williams has spoken to NME about this “real labour of love” debut solo album ‘Life Of Me And You’ and plans for the future. Check out details along with the groove-driven single ‘Hollow Man’ below. Due for release on Friday February 26, 2027, ‘Life Of Me And You’ is the guitarist’s first record released under his own name away from Manchester indie royalty Doves, Sub Sub, and Black Rivers, the band he formed in 2012 with his twin brother and bandmate Andy Williams. It also follows the Williams brothers stepping into the roles of frontmen for all tour dates after 2024’s acclaimed ‘ Constellations For The Lonely ‘ after Jimi Goodwin stepped back from the road to focus on his mental health. Described as “a deeply introspective and musically adventurous album influenced by Lou Reed, UFOs, sassy ’60s pop stars, Balearic chill and ‘slow disco'”, the record comes teased by the AC/DC meets glam psych stomp of ‘Hollow Man’ – a song inspired by the “tsunamis of information” in this digital age of “too much information, too many opinions, too much, change coming from all angles”. “I’ve been chipping away at this album in between Doves albums and tours, so it’s been a real labour of love,” Williams told NME . “I really like expressing myself in a different way. I mean, I can do the psych-melancholy listeners might expect of me and Doves all day long, but I just wanted to go into a different space. “I wanted to make something that was very personal to me that other people would enjoy and identify with, so I needed to do this solo album for me. It’s kind of like I didn’t have a choice. I just had to do it. I had to get it out of my system, and I’m very proud of it.” Check out the rest of our interview with Williams below, where he also opened up about album inspiration, his debut solo performances supporting Elbow in Manchester to celebrate ‘Asleep In The Back ‘, and what the future holds for Doves. NME : Hello Jez. How does it feel to have made something under your own name without Jimi or Andy? Jez Williams : “Yeah, it feels great. Doves’ process can be quite a sprawling one. I’ve written a lot of tunes for Doves that then go through the filter of Andy and Jimi, so there’s also been a lot of ideas that I wanted to explore on my own. “In a way, there’s a similar process involved in anything I write and record. But I was in a different headspace with my own stuff, and I wanted to go into that headspace consciously. I didn’t want it to end up sounding remotely Doves-like, whilst it still being me and probably appealing to our listeners, but I worked really intensely on creating my own sound.” Did the act of stepping up as frontman on recent Doves tours give you a certain confidence that fed into this project? “Definitely. Obviously, with Jimi not being well, we were faced with a stark decision about whether or not to go out on the road. eef3628279ba.summary_en: ドイツを拠点に活動するプログレッシブ・メタル／オルタナティヴ・メタル・バンドChaosbayが、新曲「Egosystem」をリリースしました。緻密でテクニカルなリフワークとダイナミックな重低音、そしてエレクトロニックな質感を巧みに融合させた重厚なメタルコア・サウンドを展開しており、現代社会の歪みやエゴイズムをテーマにした刺激的でメッセージ性の高い楽曲に仕上がっています。 併せて公開された公式ミュージックビデオは、楽曲が持つダークで洗練された世界観とダイナミズムを視覚的に表現した映像作品となっています。バンドの持つ鋭いアグレッションと叙情的なメロディのコントラストを強調するシネマティックな演出が施されており、Chaosbayの圧倒的な演奏力とモダン・メタルシーンにおける存在感を強く印象づける一作です。
